Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:10:1.hebrew: אומן - כגון ספר, שהכל באים אצלו ערב הרגל ורואים שאבדה לו אבידה, ואנוס הוא ואינו יכול לספר עצמו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:10:1.english: A craftsman - For example, a barber, to whom everyone comes on the eve of the Festival and sees that he has lost an item, and he is under duress and cannot cut his own hair:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:10:2.hebrew: כי הנך - דמתניתין, דקתני מגלחין, דמידע לכל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:10:2.english: Like those - of the Mishnah, which teaches that [they] may cut their hair, [where the reason] is known to everyone:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:11:1.hebrew: מפני שיצא שלא ברשות - כלומר, הואיל ולא יצא ברשות אחרים אלא ברצון עצמו, לאו אנוס הוא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:11:1.english: Because he left without permission - That is, since he did not leave with the permission of others, but of his own will, he is not [considered] constrained:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:1.hebrew: לשוט - אם יצא שלא לצורך, ולא יצא אלא כדי לשוט בעולם ולראותו, וחזר במועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:1.english: To travel - If he left without need, and left only in order to travel about the world and see it, and returned during the Festival [intermediate days]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:2.english: All agree that it is prohibited - to shave during the Festival [intermediate days]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:3.hebrew: למזונות - שיצא לחזר אחר מזונות, שאין לו מזונות, וחזר במועד אחריהן, דברי הכל מותר לגלח במועד, לפי שיצא באונס:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:3.english: For sustenance - [This refers to one] who went out to seek sustenance, because he had no food, and returned during the Festival [intermediate days] after [obtaining] it: all agree that it is permitted to shave during the Festival, because he left under duress.

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:4.hebrew: להרויחא - שיש לו נכסים הרבה, ויוצא כדי להרויח יותר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:12:4.english: For profit - [This refers to one] who has many possessions, and goes out in order to profit more:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:13:1.hebrew: נראין לי דברי רבי יהודה - דאסר בגילוח לבא ממדינת הים, כשיצא שלא ברשות:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:13:1.english: The statements of Rabbi Yehuda seem [correct] to me - who prohibited cutting [the hair] for one who comes from overseas, when he left without permission:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:13:2.hebrew: ודברי חכמים - הם דברי המתירין את התספורת כשיצא ברשות:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:13:2.english: And the statement of the Rabbis - [is the statement of] those who permit [cutting hair] when he left with permission:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:13:3.hebrew: אילימא לשוט - דקאמר רבי: נראין דברי ר"י ביצא לשוט, דהיינו שלא ברשות. הא אמרת וכו' שדברי הכל אסור, ומאי נראין דברי רבי יהודה? הלא שניהם מודים בה! אלא פשיטא להרווחא, ואשמעינן דנראין לו דברי ר' יהודה שאוסר בגילוח:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:13:3.english: If you say [it means] to travel - For Rabbi said: "The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem [correct] when he went out to travel," which is [the case of] without permission. But you said, etc. [that all agree it is prohibited]; so what does "the words of Rabbi Yehuda seem [correct]" mean? Surely both of them agree about it! Rather, it is obviously [referring to going out] for profit, and he is teaching us that the words of Rabbi Yehuda, who prohibits [him] from cutting his hair, seem [correct] to him:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:14:1.hebrew: והא נראין דברי רבי יהודה בהא - וקשיא דרבי אדרבי, דברישא נראה לו דברי ר"י דאסר בהרווחא, ובסיפא נראה לו דברי חכמים דמתירין הרווחא. אלא ודאי איכא למשמע מהכא דלאו הכי הוא כדקאמרת, דבלשוט ובמזונות פליגי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:14:1.english: But didn't you say that the statement of Rabbi Yehudah seems [more reasonable] in this [case]? - And this is a difficulty, [as it is] a contradiction of Rabbi [Yehudah the Prince's view] against [itself]: in the first clause, the statement of Rabbi Yehudah, who prohibits in a case of profit, seems [more reasonable] to him, and in the latter clause, the statement of the Rabbis, who permit in a case of profit, seems [more reasonable] to him. Rather, certainly one must infer from here that it is not as you said, [but] that they dispute [the case of one who left] to travel [for pleasure] and for sustenance:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:15:1.hebrew: ה"ק - לאו היתר דידיה אשמעינן, ולא "רואה אני" קאמר, אלא פלוגתייהו קמ"ל, במאי פליגי: נראין דברי ר"י האוסר לחכמים, וכו':
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:15:1.english: This is what [he] is saying - He is not teaching us his own [ruling of] permission, and he did not say "I see [it this way]"; rather, he is teaching us their dispute — in what [case] they disagree: The words of Rabbi Yehuda, who prohibits, seem [correct] to the Rabbis, etc.:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:16:1.hebrew: קטן הנולד במועד - ולו שערות גדולים, מותר לגלח במועד שער ראשו של הקטן, המצערו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:16:1.english: A baby born on a Festival - and he has long hair, it is permitted to cut on the Festival the hair of his head [the baby's], which is bothering him:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:16:2.hebrew: שאין לך בית האסורין גדול מזה - ממעי אמו, שהיה שם, ואנוס הוא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:16:2.english: For there is no greater prison than this - [meaning] from his mother's womb, where he was [confined], and he was [thus] prevented [from having his hair cut before the Festival]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:16:3.hebrew: מעיקרא לא - דאם נולד קודם הרגל, אינו מגלח ברגל, הואיל והיה יכול לגלח קודם הרגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:16:3.english: Beforehand, no - For if he was born before the Festival, he may not cut his hair on the Festival, since he could have cut it before the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:6:1.hebrew: אבדה לו אבידה - שלא היה לו פנאי לגלח קודם הרגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:6:1.english: He lost an item - [meaning] that he did not have time to cut his hair before the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:6:2.hebrew: דלא מוכחא מילתא - דלא ידעי כולי עלמא דאנוס היה, אלא יאמרו: הוא מכוין להשהות עד המועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:6:2.english: That the matter is not evident - That everyone does not know that he was constrained [by circumstances], but rather they will say: He intentionally delayed [cutting his hair and laundering his clothes] until the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:7:1.hebrew: יאמרו כל הסריקין אסורין וכו' - כלומר, דבייתוס היה יכול לסרוק חלותיו בלי שהות, לפי שהיה לו דפוס, ואעפ"כ אסרו, משום דאמרי: כל הסריקים כו'. הכא נמי, כיון דלא מיגליא לכולי עלמא אונסיה, יאמרו כולי עלמא: אסורין לגלח, וזה מותר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:7:1.english: They would say: All the decorated cakes are forbidden, etc. - That is to say, Baitos was able to decorate his cakes without delay, because he had a mold, and nevertheless they prohibited it, because [people] would say: All the decorated cakes [are forbidden, but the cakes of Baitos are permitted]. Here too, since his constraint is not revealed to everyone, everyone would say: [Others] are forbidden to cut their hair, but this one is permitted:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:8:1.hebrew: מי שאין לו אלא חלוק אחד - גם שם נמי לאו מוכחא מילתא לכולי עלמא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:8:1.english: One who has only one shirt - there too, the matter is not evident to everyone [that this is the reason for the leniency]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:9:1.hebrew: איזורו מוכיח עליו - דמי שאין לו אלא חלוק אחד, פושטו ומתעטף במקטרינו, וחוגרו באיזורו, ועומד ומכבס את החלוק, ומודיע לכל שאין לו אלא חלוק אחד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14a:9:1.english: His belt is proof for him - For one who has only one shirt takes it off, wraps himself in his outer cloak [mekatrino], and girds it with his belt, and stands and launders the shirt, and thereby informs everyone that he has only one shirt:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:10:1.hebrew: אומן שאבדה לו אבידה ערב הרגל - פירש בקונטרס דבאומן מבעי' ליה, אבל בני העיר, אע"פ שאין להם אומן אחר, לא מיבעיא ליה, דפשיטא דאסורים. יש להסתפק אם חלה ונתרפא, אם מותר לגלח, אם מוכחא מילתא כי הני:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:10:1.english: A craftsman who lost an item on the eve of the Festival - [Rashi] explained in his commentary that the question is raised only about a craftsman; but regarding the townspeople, even if they have no other craftsman, it is not raised, since it is obvious that they are prohibited. One may be uncertain [about a case where a person] fell ill and recovered, whether he is permitted to cut his hair — whether the matter is evident, like these [cases in the mishna]:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:11:1.hebrew: דלא כר"י - תימה, לוקמא אפילו כר"י ולמזונות, אפי' רבי יהודה מודה! ושמא כיון דקתני "ר"י אומר: הבא וכו'", משמע שבא לחלוק על המשנה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:11:1.english: [The mishna] is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - It is surprising: let us establish [the mishna] even according to Rabbi Yehuda, and [as referring] to [cutting hair] for sustenance, [for] even Rabbi Yehuda concedes! Perhaps, since [the baraita] teaches, "Rabbi Yehuda says: One who comes etc.," it implies that he came to disagree with the mishna:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:14:1.hebrew: אלא להרווחא והא אמרת נראין דברי ר"י בהא - נראה דל"ג "ועוד מכלל דפליגי רבנן אפילו למזונות". ובההיא פ"ק דשחיטת חולין (דף יב.) "נראין דברי רבי יהודה שמצאה באשפה", ל"ג "ועוד":
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:14:1.english: Rather, for profit — but didn't you say that the words of Rabbi Yehuda seem [correct] in this [case] - It seems that we do not have the reading "and furthermore, it follows that the Rabbis dispute even regarding sustenance." And in that passage in the first chapter of [tractate] Shechitat Chullin (12a), "The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem [correct] where she found it in the rubbish," we do not have the reading "and furthermore":

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:1:1.hebrew: ומנודה וכו' ושנשאל - בירושל' מקשה: הני למה התירו? והלא פשע, שלא בא לפני המועד לפני חכמים להתיר לו! ומשני: שכלו לו שלשים יום של נדוי במועד, דאין נדוי פחות משלשים יום. וכן מי שנשאל לחכם, מוקי לה כשבא בחול המועד, אי נמי לפני המועד לא מצאו בו פתח. וגילוח הראש נמי אסור במועד, דהא אמר בגמ' שלא יכנסו לרגל מנוולין, ואין לך ניוול גדול מזה. ושמא לא קאי טעמא בגמרא אלא אשארא; אבל גילוח של ראשו אסור משום מלאכה, אפילו במקום אונס. ושאר גילוח דבעי בגמרא מאי טעמא אסורין, והיינו גילוח של יפוי, דהוה לך למישרי לצורך המועד אע"פ שהיא מלאכה; אבל גילוח כל הראש אסור משום מלאכה, והני כגון נזיר ומצורע הוא דשרי משום מצוה. ולפי זה אסור לגלח ראשו במועד. ועוד יש לפרש שנראה שמותר לגלח ראשו במועד. וא"ת מאי קא משמע לן נזיר ומצורע? יש לומר דס"ד דאסור, שלא ישהו קרבנותיהן, קא משמע לן דשרי. ואי מיירי הכא בשלא היה להן פנאי דוקא, והוא כדבעי למימר בגמרא, יש לומר דהכי קאמר: דנזיר ומצורע העולין מטומאה לטהרה דוקא שעולין עתה, אבל עולין מטומאה לטהרה מקודם רגל אסורין:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:1:1.english: And one who was ostracized, etc., and one who requested [release from a vow] - The Jerusalem Talmud asks: Why did they permit these? Didn't he act negligently, in that he did not come before the Festival to the Sages to have it permitted for him? And it answers: [This refers to one] whose thirty days of ostracism were completed during the Festival, for ostracism is not less than thirty days. And similarly, [regarding] one who requested [release] from a Sage, it establishes it [as a case where he] came during the intermediate days of the Festival, or alternatively, before the Festival [but] they did not find an opening [for release] for him. And shaving the head is also forbidden on the Festival, for [the Gemara] said that they should not enter the Festival disheveled, and there is no greater disheveling than this. But perhaps the reason [stated] in the Gemara applies only to the rest [of the hair]; but shaving his head is forbidden because of [the prohibition of] labor, even in a case of duress. And as for the other shaving about which the Gemara asks, "What is the reason they are forbidden?" — that is, shaving for beautification, which you should have permitted for the need of the Festival even though it is labor; but shaving the entire head is forbidden because of labor, and these, such as a nazirite and a leper, it is [only] permitted because of a mitzvah. And according to this, it is forbidden to shave one's head on the Festival. Furthermore, it can be explained that it appears that it is permitted to shave one's head on the Festival. And if you say: What does [the Mishnah] teach us [by mentioning] a nazirite and a leper? One can say that you might have thought it forbidden, so that they not delay their offerings; it teaches us that it is permitted. And if [the Mishnah] here speaks only of [those] who did not have time [beforehand], and this is as the Gemara wished to say, one can say that this is what it is saying: that [it refers] only to a nazirite and a leper who are ascending from impurity to purity [and] who ascend now; but those who ascended from impurity to purity before the Festival are forbidden:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:3:1.hebrew: ושאר כל אדם מאי טעמא אסורין - אע"פ שהוא מלאכה, היה לנו להתירה לצורך המועד. א"נ, אפילו אם נאמר [אף] שיש מלאכות אסורות במועד שאין בהן טורח, כגון פרקמטיא, מכל מקום זה שהוא ליפוי ראוי להתיר לכבוד מועד. ויש מפרשים דקאי על גילוח הראש, דאסרינן משום טירחא, מכל מקום מקשה דהיה לו להתיר לצורך המועד. ואין זה נוטה לפי מה שפירש' רש"י המשנה, דגילוח כל הראש מלאכה גמורה ואסור:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:3:1.english: And all other people, what is the reason that they are prohibited - Even though it is [an act of] labor, we should have permitted it for the needs of the Festival. Alternatively, [even if we say] that there are labors that are prohibited on the Festival even though they involve no toil, such as commerce, nevertheless this [act], which is for beautification, should be permitted in honor of the Festival. And some explain that [the question] refers to shaving the head, which we prohibit because of the toil [involved]; nevertheless, [the Gemara] asks that it should have been permitted for the needs of the Festival. But this does not accord with what [Rashi] explained [in] the Mishnah, that shaving the entire head is full-fledged labor and is prohibited:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:8:1.hebrew: שאין לו אלא חלוק אחד מותר לכבסו במועד - ואם תאמר: היאך יכבסנו במועד? אם כן ישאר במועד בלא חלוק בשעת כיבוס! כמו כן היה יכול לכבס קודם המועד, ויהיה בלא חלוק בשעת כיבוס. וכי תימא: כשכבסו קודם מועד, ומשום הכי מותר לכבסו במועד, א"כ תרתי נמי, אם יתלכלכו, למה נאסור לו? והלא לא פשע! י"ל דדי לו בשתי חלוקין, אחד ליו"ט ראשון ואחד לי"ט אחרון. בירושלמי אמרו: בגדי קטנים מותר לכבסן במועד, דניכרים שהם קטנים ומלוכלכין כמי שאין לו אלא חלוק אחד:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14a:8:1.english: One who has only one shirt is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of the Festival - And if you say: How may he launder it on the intermediate days? If so, he will remain without a shirt during the intermediate days at the time of the laundering! Likewise, he could have laundered before the Festival, and be without a shirt at the time of the laundering. And if you say: [This is permitted] when he laundered it before the Festival, and therefore it is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days — if so, [one who has] two [shirts] too, if they become soiled, why should we forbid it to him? Surely he was not negligent! One can answer that two shirts are enough for him, one for the first Yom Tov and one for the last Yom Tov. In the Jerusalem Talmud they said: Children's clothes are permitted to be laundered on the intermediate days, because it is evident that they are children's [clothes], and they are soiled like [the clothes of] one who has only one shirt:
